label: D1 after a1->S1 rewarded, strongest when the trial before was unrewarded or reached S2
short_terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("state", -2) == 2)
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("action", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * belief_cover ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo
explanation: Active only at D1 (zero at GO and D2). Its magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a1 -> S1 rewarded (common, rewarded at S1); every other previous-trial pattern sits about 0.09 below the timing baseline. Within a1 S1 r it is graded by what came before: biggest (about 1.5-1.7) when the trial before that was unrewarded, especially an a1 -> S2 rare unrewarded trial, and it shrinks over a run of consecutive S1 rewards (about 1.7, 1.3, 0.9). So it looks like a response to a newly rewarded S1 more than to a settled S1 belief. The ideal-observer belief_lo adds little on its own once the a1 S1 r indicator is in. The free fit adds: lower if the trial before was a2, or unrewarded at S1, plus a small boost when the trial three back was unrewarded. Window-start trials (where the trial two back is unknown) fire less, and that is not captured. The observed ceiling (all observed) is 0.29, so a large part of the variance is out of reach for observed additive cues.
